title: Enterprise Ask Gate and Minimum Deliverable Matrix
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a decision gate and a standardized "minimum deliverable" matrix for incoming Sales/CS enterprise feature requests to speed triage, produce repeatable initial scoping, and give predictable handoffs to Engineering and Solutions. This ticket produces a one-page scoring rubric, tier definitions (Quick Win / Core Integration / Dedicated Offering / Custom Eng Engagement), and a short template that CS can use during first contact.
background: Sales and CS receive a large volume of enterprise asks that vary widely in technical complexity and required product changes. PMs currently spend inconsistent time on first-pass scoping; some asks are over-scoped while others lack needed compliance checks. This creates friction in prioritization, long feedback loops to customers, and surprises in implementation effort and cost. We need a lightweight gate that standardizes the first 30 minutes of scoping and outputs a recommended tier and an initial list of engineering touchpoints.
goal: Reduce time-to-first-response for enterprise asks to under 48 hours, standardize initial scoping outputs so engineering can estimate within ±40% confidence for tiered work, and reduce re-scope cycles after handoff by 30% in Q2.
scope_in_scope: Scoring rubric for first-pass prioritization (security, infra, revenue, complexity)
Four-tier minimum deliverable matrix with test prompts and SLO/security checkpoints
CS Intake template (form) and two example completed intake submissions
Handoff checklist for PM -> ENG with expected artifact list (PRD sketch, sample prompts)
Simple training session + one-pager for CS and Solutions teams
out_of_scope: Building a full intake portal (this ticket produces the template and rubrics only)
Detailed engineering estimates or sprint planning (handled after handoff)
Automated routing rules in Redwood Console (future work)
decision_rubric: Score components (0-3) across: Business Value, Technical Complexity, Data Sensitivity, SLA/Uptime Requirements, Integration Surface (API/SDK), Regulatory Constraints
Priority score = weighted sum: Business Value x3, Technical Complexity x1.5, Data Sensitivity x2, SLA x2, Integration x1
Thresholds: 0-6 Quick Win, 7-11 Core Integration, 12-15 Dedicated Offering, >=16 Custom Eng Engagement
Must-block flags: 'Requires customer-managed on-prem deployment' OR 'Data cannot leave customer network' => automatic escalation to Private/Legal review
mvp_tiers: Quick Win: small product change or console toggle; deliverable = short PRD sketch + one example prompt + acceptance test; target engineering latency: 1-2 s of triage before sign-off
Core Integration: new API param or model routing rule; deliverable = scoping doc with API contract, sample data, minimal security checklist; requires cross-team review (ENG+Infra)

Dedicated Offering: reserved capacity / dedicated model variant for a customer; deliverable = runbook, cost estimate, dedicated infra checklist, rollout plan; requires Solutions + Sales contract input
Custom Eng Engagement: bespoke on-prem or deep product changes; deliverable = full implementation brief, compliance sign-off, SOW placeholder; requires legal, security, and architecture reviews
acceptance_criteria: One-page scoring rubric published to Confluence and linked in the CS intake playbook
Three completed example intake forms that map real recent asks to the matrix (anonymized)
CS Intake template shared and tested with at least two channel reps
Handoff checklist validated in a trial with one pilot account and updated based on feedback
Metrics baseline established for current triage lead time (hours) and re-scope rate
rollout_plan: Week 1: Draft rubric and tier definitions; iterate with Solutions and two AE reps
Week 2: Produce intake template and three anonymized examples; run 60-min training with CS
Week 3: Pilot with inbound enterprise queue for two weeks; collect handoff feedback
Week 4: Update artifacts, publish Confluence page, add playbook link to CS handbook; schedule follow-up retro
metrics: Engineering re-scope rate after first handoff (target -30% vs baseline)
Percent of asks correctly tiered vs final implementation (target >75% accuracy)
CS satisfaction with intake flow (survey after pilot, target >= 4/5)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-simplified rubric mis-classifies complex asks => Mitigation: require mandatory field for 'unknowns' and a low-effort tech spike flag
Risk: CS adoption low => Mitigation: embed template in existing CS workflow and run 1:1 office hours
Risk: Security/regulatory blindspots => Mitigation: include mandatory security checklist items and an explicit escalation path to Security team
Risk: Sales pushes to classify as Quick Win for faster responses => Mitigation: tie classification to pre-defined SLA and require PM sign-off for downgrades
